goal: In scripts/bench_real.py, add a stricter _readme_ok README checker and make the summarize_readme case use the docs agent and this checker.
requirements: Add a module-level function _readme_ok(a) after _has. It returns a tuple (ok, text): text is a[:100] with each newline replaced by a space. The function uses no module-level names.
ok is True only when the lowercased a contains 'mcp', contains 'local' or 'ollama', and contains one of 'router', 'dispatch', 'delegat', 'summar'.
ok is False when the lowercased a contains any of: 'openai api', 'github platform', 'could not read', 'cannot read', 'unable to read', 'unable to access', 'do not have access'.
In the summarize_readme entry of cases(), change the agent from 'support-docs-writer' to 'engineering-technical-writer', and replace the checker _has('mcp', 'local') with the bare name _readme_ok.
Change nothing else in the file; _has and the other cases stay as they are.
context: Python 3.11. The entry is a 5-element tuple: name, agent, setup, prompt, checker. Keep the file's short-line style. The checker takes the agent's answer as a str a and returns (ok, text).
